entries.proposition: The patient carries a heterozygous 6.8 Mb deletion of 16q22.2-q23.1 whose distal breakpoint lies inside WWOX.
entries.snippet: A 6.8 Mb heterozygous chromosomal deletion was detected within 16q22.2-q23.1, which contains 57 Refseq genes including PHLPP2 and WWOX

entries.proposition: Both breakpoints lie within PHLPP2 and WWOX.
entries.snippet: Both breakpoints of the deleted region were located within those genes.

entries.proposition: The other WWOX allele was examined by exon-targeted panel sequencing with coverage inspection, not by intronic, structural or RNA analysis.
entries.snippet: We conducted a targeted panel sequencing (TPS) for the targeted exons of 4813 disease-related genes

entries.proposition: No pathogenic variant was found on the other WWOX allele.
entries.snippet: no pathogenic variants were detected in the other allele of WWOX.

entries.proposition: Parental DNA was unavailable, so inheritance of the deletion is unknown.
entries.snippet: Parental DNA was unavailable; therefore, the deletion was not confirmed as occurring de novo.

entries.proposition: The authors decline to attribute the phenotype to WWOX haploinsufficiency.
entries.snippet: Thus, the relationship between haploinsufficiency of WWOX and/or other genes located around WWOX and West syndrome remains unclear

entries.proposition: Seizures stopped after valproate plus lamotrigine following phenobarbital, valproate and zonisamide.
entries.snippet: Antiepileptic drug treatment was switched to a combination of VPA and LTG,

entries.proposition: Two database cases with an overlapping maternally inherited deletion carried E17K on the other allele.
